doc.title: Germaine Bazzle interviewed by Monk Rowe, Rome, New York, August 21, 2006

title: Learning from records and from instrumentalists
summary: She learned from Ella, Sarah, Bird and Miles records, and found learning instrumentalists' solos more useful than copying vocalists.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Reading music versus faking and playing by ear

blocks.x: And the part that you were talking about doing, the clapping thing, which I think I probably will steal that by the way because — it’s funny when people start clapping on one and three, I sometimes don’t know how to deal with that. So I love your — ask them which feels better. Did you have someone when you were a young person helping you learn?

Well I had records. You know those youngsters don’t know about these thirty-three and a thirds you know. But that’s what we had. And Ella Fitzgerald, Sarah Vaughan, Charlie Parker, Miles Davis. You know because we listened a lot and I told the students this this afternoon. For me to learn how to do what I do, especially with the scatting, came from © Fillius Jazz Archive -3-

listening to instrumentalists more than vocalists. As much as I enjoyed and learned from Ella and Sarah and all those ladies, at one time I had to stop listening to them because I found myself almost trying to do their things, doing their music. And I said but it’s not mine. It’s not me yet. So listening to instrumentalists and learning their solos and then learning everybody’s solo on the recording, that was the challenge. And then being able to sing those solos while you’re doing the dishes or whatever, without the recordings you see. That was the challenge. And there was a group of us in school, I mean that’s what it was. We’d sit in what we call the co-op at the university — it was like a little café or something. And we’d sit in the co-op and we’d sing these songs and okay, you take Bird’s solo, you take Miles’ solo and it was great fun. It was great fun. I never imagined I would be using it now but at the time I mean I just liked jazz and you just sing it. But I never thought I’d be using it in this manner.
